agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The scan confirms 6176 and 6508 as by far the strongest AND(chat, math) units in layers 0–17: 8.1 and 4.2 sd, against at most about 2.8 for anything else. A second tier sits right after them, in layers 12–13 (L12 n6233, n4689, n159; L13 n754, n2476; about 1.7–2.8 sd). Those may simply be downstream echoes of 6176/6508, or parallel readers of the same upstream trigger. Nothing before layer 11 shows the pattern, so the AND is first computed at layer 11. Layer 11 is a full-attention layer and its attention wrote the large chat-specific offset. Its heads can see both the chat tokens and the problem, so I'd guess the trigger enters through layer-11 attention and the neurons' nonlinearity forms the AND. As a weight-only check, I'll measure how much each layer-11 attention head's output space (o_proj slice, post-attention norm scaling) overlaps the effective input rows (gate and up, with pre-FF norm scaling) of 6176 and 6508, compared with random neurons. A single head with outsized overlap would be the natural upstream target.

Head 3 of layer 11 stands out. Both gate neurons' up rows overlap its output space at 0.66 and 0.64, against 0.40 ± 0.07 for random neurons (about 3.5 sd), and their gate rows also lean toward head 3 (0.51 and 0.57). Earlier attention patterns (fwd_12) showed that the same head, L11h3, takes 30–40% of its attention from the chat-template tokens. That fits it as the channel bringing the "this is a chat" signal into these neurons. Hypothesis: L11h3 attends to the chat tokens and writes a signal that, combined with math content in the residual, switches on 6176 and 6508 (and possibly the layer-12/13 second tier). For a causal test, I'll zero head 3's o_proj columns (768–1023) in layer 11 and run a teacher-forced pass on the same tf10 texts with MLP activations at layers 11–13. If the hypothesis holds, 6176 and 6508 in v0 should collapse toward their v3 and chat levels. If they stay near −2.9 and −2.0, head 3 is not the trigger.

The diagnostic edit is in place. Head 3's o_proj slice holds a large share of the tensor's norm (relative change 0.69), so it is the dominant head in layer 11's output. I'll run the teacher-forced pass with the edited model.

Head 3 of layer 11 is now zeroed. I'll compare the response-token means of 6176, 6508 and the second-tier layer-12/13 AND units between the original (fwd_18) and this edited pass, in each group (v0, v3, chat). I'll also compare the mean solution logprob per group to see the overall cost of removing the head.
